object: base of a kneeling granite ram (statue), inscribed round the base
notes: Meroitic hieroglyphic type, read right to left (signs face left); [x] = Griffith's restoration (blanked in text_corpus and not counted in signs), x? after a sign = Griffith's '?' or a half-bracketed trace. Three printed lines; line 1 holds a cartouche (lost start + reqerem), followed by an Egyptian ankh sign with Griffith's '?' and a raised dot, both left out of the text. Lacunae are Griffith's dots, one [.] per dot (he estimates about seven signs lost before the cartouche's r). Griffith: the cartouche falls into two halves, '...re' and Qerem (title of the deceased on Kar. 45); qore follows the cartouche ('I have noted space only for one sign at the corner'); mnitkel = the royal title Amanitakel, as at Kalabsha 94/1; pwrite : lḫte is a phrase like those after divine names at Naga (nos. 6 ff.); then the name of Ammon (amn...). His restoration of the end (not transcribed): 'pwrite : lḫ[te] : amn[....]teli : [mlowi : yi]tbḫ[te] :'. Copies of Duemichen 1863 and Ward collated with the original in January 1910; photographs Pls. XV, XVI. Cross-check: FHN III gives the Son of Rê name on this ram as Mnhreqerem (REM 0001), which ends in the reqerem read here right to left.

object: two cartouches beside a rock relief of a king and the sun-god
notes: Meroitic hieroglyphic type, read right to left (signs face left); [x] = Griffith's restoration (blanked in text_corpus and not counted in signs), x? after a sign = Griffith's '?' or a half-bracketed trace. Printed as two vertical cartouches, read top to bottom, right cartouche first; within a row of two signs the right one first. Each cartouche is topped by two flat signs with dots under them, not read. Left cartouche: a hatched (lost) block at the top, written as one [.]. All '?' are Griffith's. Griffith: 'hardly legible on the small photograph. The signs face to the right in the original. Most are doubtful; if the first cartouche is rightly read, it is the name of the prince at Amara (see Part II., no. 84), but the reading is too uncertain to serve as the basis for any argument.' Photograph Pl. XIV, fig. 2. Cross-check: FHN III reads the Gebel Qeili names as Sorkrr (Son of Rê name) and Mnslhe (throne name), REM 0002, and the same king's name as Sorkror at Amara (REM 0084), which confirms that the right cartouche is Griffith's 'first'; Griffith's type has an extra ḫ and o in it, and the second cartouche differs from Mnslhe.

object: pylon, left (south) tower, three columns in front of and above the king
notes: Meroitic hieroglyphic type, read right to left (signs face left); [x] = Griffith's restoration (blanked in text_corpus and not counted in signs), x? after a sign = Griffith's '?' or a half-bracketed trace. Griffith prints the text in three parts: the first side line, the central cartouche (with an Egyptian bee title and two flat signs above it, not read), and the third side line. The side lines are the same on both towers ('all these letters except m being visible on either side'; the m 'is from my collation, but is not well supported by the photograph'); he reads the first as 'in ... mte' and says the third line is as in nos. 6 and 7. The divider in the third line is printed in round brackets. In the cartouche a horizontal rule marks the joint between a worn upper block and a better lower block, and three dots mark a gap. The king's name on the upper block (ntkm) is Griffith's proposed restoration, printed without brackets in his type and bracketed here: Natakamani's and Amanitere's names 'would suit the lacunae admirably... A careful examination with a good ladder might establish these readings, for which there seems in fact some justification in the photograph of the cartouche on the left.' The title below: 'The king's name was thus followed by his title qêrê (or qore)'. Breasted photos 506, 507; L., D., V., Bl. 56; Pl. XVII.

object: royal cartouches (king, queen, prince) before the royalties on the south wall, signs in relief
notes: Meroitic hieroglyphic type, read right to left (signs face left); [x] = Griffith's restoration (blanked in text_corpus and not counted in signs), x? after a sign = Griffith's '?' or a half-bracketed trace. Griffith: nos. 5, 6 and 9 on the south wall have the signs in relief on a sunk ground; the prince's cartouches 'are preserved only on the back and south walls'.

object: caption of the lion-headed god (Apedemak), south wall, relief
notes: Meroitic hieroglyphic type, read right to left (signs face left); [x] = Griffith's restoration (blanked in text_corpus and not counted in signs), x? after a sign = Griffith's '?' or a half-bracketed trace. Text kept in Griffith's printed order. Griffith: 'In the above readings the order of the columns is disregarded in order to bring together the parallel phrases in the different inscriptions, putting the distinctive name of the deity at the beginning.' His superscript stone-column numbers are kept as '(n)' where they fall, so the stone order can be rebuilt by sorting the segments. Griffith: the gods and goddesses alike have pwrite : lbḫte, the gods also mlowi : yitebḫte, the goddesses ntke : lbḫte; 'A careful revision with the original would no doubt confirm or correct many doubtful readings' (copies collated from a ladder, January 1910). A raised dot printed inside pw-r-ite in several captions is left out. Griffith: the name of the lion-god (Apezemak) must probably be restored, 'but whether with initial a, as in 18, is not certain. There seems hardly room for this.' Nos. 5, 6 and 9 have the signs in relief on a sunk ground. L., D., V., 62; Breasted photos 515, 516.

site: Naga, temple of Ammon (Lepsius's temple d)
notes: Meroitic hieroglyphic type, read right to left (signs face left); [x] = Griffith's restoration (blanked in text_corpus and not counted in signs), x? after a sign = Griffith's '?' or a half-bracketed trace. The standard texts of the Amun temple are printed once on p. 63 and assigned by Griffith to several numbers; this row carries the printed text, not a separate copy. Griffith: 'The standard inscription with the human-headed form is given twice in 23, 36, and once in 37... The name Amani is followed by a group which might mean "in Nête", i.e. perhaps Ne (Thebes) or Napata. The next is the name of Khons in no. 9 above... The last word is made up of well-known elements.' The royal cartouches before the royalties carry Egyptian prenomens and titles (not transcribed) with the Meroitic names, printed on p. 63 as ntkmni (king), mnitore (queen) and arkḫtna (prince, 'Araka-khatani'; final a as printed, where no. 34 and FHN III have Arkhtni). They are not in text_std: Griffith gives them once for the doorways, not per number, though FHN III counts them in REM 0023, 0024, 0027, 0029, 0031, 0033-0038. L., D., V., 60a; Breasted photo 532; Pls. XXI, XXII (Pl. XXII copies 23, 24).
